column1: # catalog-space.tsv -- general (non-developer) reclaim candidates.
# Anything also listed in catalog-dev.tsv is excluded at runtime and summarised
# as a single pointer to /clean-dev, so no path is ever proposed by two skills.
# Columns: subcategory, path, select, risk, method, undo, why
#   select   self            the path itself is the candidate
#            children        each immediate child is a separate candidate
#            older:<days>    children untouched for at least N days
#            ext:a,b,c       children with one of these extensions
# `children` matters: offering "~/Library/Caches, 8.5 GB" as one checkbox is how
# a cleaner ends up deleting a running app's live data. Caches are per
# application, so the decision is per application.
# Note what is deliberately absent: system and user logs, language files,
# universal binary slices, and "broken" preference plists. docs/WHY-NOT.md
# explains each omission.
user-caches
column7: Cache for one application. macOS reclaims caches on its own under disk pressure, so removing them buys little and costs that app a slower next launch.

column1: trash-main
column7: Items already in the Trash. Emptying it is what actually returns space that earlier cleans only moved.

column1: downloads-stale
column7: Untouched for at least 180 days. User data, so it is shown for your decision and never selected for you.

column1: installer-dmg
column7: Installer disk image or package. Almost always re-downloadable from the vendor.

column1: ios-backups
column7: iOS device backups. Shown for visibility only: this is often the only copy of a phone, so cmai will not remove it.

column1: mail-downloads
column7: Mail attachment copy. Safe only for IMAP accounts where the server still holds the message; for POP or local-only mail these exist nowhere else.

column1: quicklook-thumbs
column7: Quick Look thumbnail cache; regenerated on demand.

column1: crashreports
column7: Crash report older than 90 days. Useful evidence while you are still diagnosing something, disposable long afterwards.

column1: saved-state
column7: Window and document restore state for one application. Losing it means that app reopens empty, nothing more.
